calls.head: The Wild’s power play has a target
calls.body: The Islanders’ penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Wild’s power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Islanders tonight.

calls.head: Tilted ice, toward the Islanders’ net
calls.body: The Wild have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Islanders near the bottom. Expect the Wild to spend more of the night in the Islanders’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

calls.head: The Islanders’ defense joins the attack, the Wild’s stays home
calls.body: On shots from defensemen, the Islanders are the league’s best, but Minnesota is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Islanders’ defensemen jump into the play.

NYI.head: We gave the Islanders only a 28% chance, and they proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Minnesota couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: The Islanders usually give up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: Minnesota’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.5% (about 6.8% against the Islanders) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 350 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Schaefer plays hero in overtime
paras: Joel Eriksson Ek got the scoring started for the Wild just 27 seconds into the game. The Islanders’ Ryan Pulock left early in the first period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with an upper-body injury. Matthew Schaefer tied it 1-1 for the Islanders late in the period, and Bo Horvat put the Islanders ahead 2-1 on the power play early in the second. Quinn Hughes tied it 2-2 for Minnesota late in the period. Adam Pelech restored the Islanders’ lead early in the third, but Matt Boldy tied it up for Minnesota with just under four minutes left. Schaefer won it with his second goal of the night 33 seconds into overtime. He added an assist for a three-point night.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Ilya Sorokin made 22 saves for the Islanders, and Jesper Wallstedt stopped 22 of 26 at the other end. The Isles improved to 7-4-2 and climbed to fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Wild dropped to 9-3-3, still first in the Central.

items.text: The Wild’s three-game winning streak is over.
Maxim Shabanov played his first game against the Islanders since leaving.
Matthew Schaefer has a point in six straight games.

The Islanders won without Mathew Barzal, Matias Maccelli, Alexander Romanov and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Maple Leafs were missing more at the time.
